text:
Person: Please send the invitations for our office party.
Assistant: Happy to. Which day is the party?
Person: Next Friday at six. We will set up tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Got it. Who should get the invitation?
Person: Everyone on the team list. Add a note that we will roast chicken and vegetables, so it will be delicious.
Assistant: Done. I sent the invitation to the team list for Friday at six, with your note about the roast.
Person: Can you also find my lost ring? I think I dropped it at the last party.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't find lost things. You could ask the place where the party was if they have it.

Sam is a student who shares a flat, and the power bill had been too high. He picked up his phone and said, "Show me how much electricity we used this week, but I don't want the whole year, just the last seven days." The assistant understood that he wanted a short report, not a long one. It opened the energy app and showed a small chart. Sam saw that the heater used the most power. He said, "Turn the heater down to eighteen, and don't touch the lights." The assistant lowered the heater and left the lights as they were. Sam gave a little wave to his flatmate on the sofa and said the room would be cooler now. Then he asked the phone to remind him on Sunday to move some money from his bank account to pay the bill. The assistant set a reminder for Sunday evening and said it was done.

name: bus_arrival_check
does: Tells you how many minutes until the next bus will stop at your stop.
inputs: the bus number and the name of the stop
people say:
- When does my bus come?
- Is the 42 almost here? It is rainy and I don't want to wait outside.
- How long until the next bus at Park Street?
- Tell me if the bus is running late.
- I'm sitting by the socket in the station cafe. How long until the 8 bus is outside?

Someone wants to book a haircut.
Haircut, please.
Book me a trim.
I need my hair cut this week.
Can you count me in for a haircut on Saturday morning?
Is there a slot open for a medium trim, about half an hour?
Find me a barber with more free times than the last one.
Please book a haircut for one person, and nothing too short.
I would be very grateful if you could book me a cut at the shop near my office, because my hair is getting long and I have a photo next week.

Lena was running late and her bus left in five minutes. She grabbed her bag and called out to the smart speaker, "Turn off the kitchen lights and dim the hall lamp to the least bright setting, please." The speaker understood both things. It switched off the kitchen lights and set the hall lamp to ten percent. Lena wanted her dog to feel calm while she was out, so she added, "And play soft music in the living room." The assistant started a quiet playlist. Just then the old bulb in the bedroom gave a small crack and went dark. Lena sighed. "Remind me to buy a new bulb tonight," she said. The assistant set the reminder for seven in the evening and told her it was saved. Lena ran out the door and caught her bus with a minute to spare.

A trip to the post office is a common errand. People go there to send parcels, buy stamps, or pick up something that was left when they were out. If you carry a suitcase or a big box, you may need a bigger label. Before you leave, you can ask your assistant to find the nearest post office, or to check when it opens. People say things like "Where can I post this?" or "Is the post office open now?" If the address on a parcel is wrong, you can ask the shop to fix it before it goes. You might also say "Move my pickup to Friday" when you can't be home. Small changes like the day, the time or the place are easy to ask for, as long as you say them plainly.

name: delivery_tracker
does: Shows where an order is and when it will arrive, even if the delivery has stretched past the first date.
inputs: the order number or the name of the shop
people say:
- Where is my order?
- When will the bike arrive?
- Has my parcel left the shop yet?
- Can you see if my favourite jacket has been sent?
- How long until my delivery gets here?

Babies like a steady day. Feeding times and nap times help them feel safe, and they help parents plan. A baby may eat every three hours, and a nap may last from thirty minutes to two hours. The length of a nap changes as the baby grows. Parents often change the plan with a few simple words: "Move the next feed to six," "Make the nap shorter," or "Tell me when the baby wakes up." A baby monitor helps too. On a foggy morning, when the baby sleeps late, a parent might say, "Don't wake her yet." While the parent fries eggs in the kitchen, the monitor sends a quiet sound to the phone. People ask for small changes in plain words, like earlier, later, longer or shorter.

Someone wants to move a meeting to a later time.
Push my meeting back an hour.
Move the two o'clock to three.
Can we do it later today?
Make my meeting later.
Shift the team call to tomorrow, please.
I'd like to move my meeting with the guest speaker to Thursday.
Please change my Monday meeting to the afternoon, because I will lose the morning to a rare doctor visit that I could not book on any other day.
Could you kindly move the meeting to next week? A rare chance to see my grandmother came up, and I do not want to lose it.

Restarting a computer is one of the easiest fixes. When a screen freezes or a program is slow, you turn the computer off and start it again. This clears small problems and makes the computer quick again. Before you restart, save your files in a folder so you don't lose them. Ben's wife was happy when her old laptop worked again after a restart. People ask in many ways: "Restart my computer," "Turn it off and on," or "Start it fresh in five minutes." They also change the screen: "Make the screen brighter," "Dim it," or "Turn on battery saver." The words are simple, and the computer does what it was told.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests a few gifts for a person, based on what they like and how much you want to spend.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they enjoy, and a price limit
people say:
- What should I get my dad for his birthday?
- I need a present for my niece. She loves riding her bicycle, and I can spend about twenty dollars.
- Any ideas for a coworker? Something polite and not too personal.
- My friend is turning thirty and I have no idea what to give.
- Something small for my aunt, but no flowers, because she sneezes all the time.

Priya, an office worker, sat down at home after a long day and found the internet very slow. It was a foggy evening and the router light blinked orange. She said to her phone, "Why is the wifi so slow? Explain it to me." The assistant checked and said that six devices were using the connection, which was twice as many as usual. Priya said, "Pause the tablet and the game console." The assistant paused both, and the speed went up to nearly double. Her video call with her brother worked fine after that. On the screen she could see his picture, a yellow duck, and she laughed. Then she asked the assistant to keep the tablet paused until nine. It said that it would.

Dan was a busy parent with sticky honey on his fingers, and he was late for the school pickup. He picked up the phone with his elbow and typed, "call jenny on speakerphoen". The assistant saw the small typo and understood that he meant speakerphone. It called Jenny, who was Dan's sister, and turned on the speaker. Dan said, "Can you get Max today? I'm running late." Jenny said yes, and said they could split the week, with her taking Monday and Tuesday. After the call, Dan said, "Save a note to call Jenny back about the week." The assistant saved the note and told him it was done. Dan washed his hands and ran out to the car.

Someone wants an alarm to wake them up.
Wake me at seven.
Set an alarm for six thirty tomorrow.
I'm taking a nap, so buzz me in twenty-five minutes.
I need to get up early. My room is messy and I have to tidy it before work.
Can you set a soft alarm, one that filters in slowly instead of a loud ring?
Please make sure I am awake by eight, because I need to buy one last ingredient for the cake before the shop closes.
Alarm, seven, weekdays.

Someone wants to call back a number that just called them.
Call them back.
Ring Tom, he just called me.
Who called me? Please call them back.
I missed a call from my brother, could you call him back for me?
I'm saving data this month, so call that number back over wifi.
Call the library on their public number and remember to leave a message if nobody answers.
Call the last number that rang, and tell me who it was.
Would you mind calling the number that missed me earlier? If nobody picks up, please leave a voicemail.

Rosa was a busy parent, and her phone kept saying that the storage was full. She had only a few minutes before school. She said, "Phone, my storage is full. Upload my photos to the cloud, but only the ones from last year." The assistant said the phone was not connected to wifi, so it connected to the home network first. Then it began to upload. "How much room will that give me?" Rosa asked. The assistant said about twenty-five gigabytes. Rosa nodded and said, "Also turn on do not disturb until noon, I have a meeting." The assistant did it. Rosa packed the lunch boxes while the photos went up. When she left the house, the screen showed that the upload was finished.

Omar was a driver who had just finished a long shift. Sitting in his truck, he typed fast: "set the round hot tub to 38 degress and start the pump". The assistant read the small typo as degrees and sent both orders to the controller at home. The tub began to heat, and the pump turned on. A moment later the assistant said the water was at 31 and would reach 38 in about forty minutes. Omar said, "Call my sister." She was a nurse and had the same long hours. When she answered, he said, "Come over after your shift, the tub will be warm soon." She said she would be there at nine.

At home, the router sends wifi to your phones and computers. Each device joins with a password. The router often hangs on a hook on the wall, and a pink sticker on it may show the wifi name and password. Some routers let you filter which devices can go online, or block certain websites for children. People ask for changes in plain words: "Change the wifi password," "Block the tablet at night," or "Restart the router." If the connection is slow, people say, "The internet is slow today," and the assistant can restart the router or tell them which device is using the most.

Wifi sometimes does not reach outside the house. If the signal is weak in the garden, people say, "The internet is bad out here." Do not put the router next to the kitchen sink or behind a thick wall, because the signal gets weaker there. When friends visit, you welcome them and give them the wifi name and password. Many routers have a guest network, which is separate from your own, so visitors can go online without seeing your files. People ask for it in simple words: "Turn on the guest wifi," "Give me a new guest password," or "Turn the guest wifi off tonight."

After a family roast dinner, Mara found a big stain on her husband's orange shirt, where he had spilled beer. She was holding the baby, so she said to the kitchen speaker, "Start the washing machine on the stain cycle, and use half the usual soap. It's only one shirt." The assistant understood that she wanted the stain cycle with less soap. It started the machine and said the cycle would take fifty minutes. "Make it warmer than usual," Mara added. The assistant raised the temperature from thirty to forty degrees. Later, Mara asked it to tell her when the wash was done. The assistant sent a message to her phone right on time, and she hung the shirt up to dry.

Joe the gardener was done for the day. His hoodie was wet and he wanted to go home, but he did not remember where he had parked the car. He shouted across the garden to his phone, "Where is my car, and is it ready to go with enough fuel?" The assistant opened the car app. It said the car was on Elm Street, two minutes away on foot, and that the tank was half full. Joe said, "Start the engine and warm it up." The assistant sent the command. When Joe walked to the car, the heater was already on and the windows were clear. He took off his wet hoodie and put it on the back seat.

name: account_balance_check
does: Gives a smart, short answer about how much money is in one of your accounts, so you can double-check before you spend.
inputs: which account you mean
people say:
- How much money do I have?
- What's in my savings?
- Is my account low? I need to pay the rent.
- Does my card have enough before I buy this?
- I'm at the cash machine in my neighborhood. What is left in my account?

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap and spinning. People pick a cycle, like cotton, delicate or quick. A dryer then warms the clothes until they are dry. On a cloudy day, drying outside is slow, so many people use the dryer. A small light on the machine may blink when the wash is done or when something is wrong. After drying, folded clothes can go into a vacuum bag for winter storage. People ask for changes in simple words: "Start a quick wash," "Make it warmer," "Add ten more minutes to the dryer," or "Tell me when it's done."

Person: print 20 copies of the movie night poster plese
Assistant: Sure. Do you want them in colour or black and white?
Person: colour, and on thick paper
Assistant: I can print twenty copies in colour. The thick paper tray is empty, though. Can you fill it, or should I use normal paper?
Person: normal is fine. we want to put them up before we paint the shop window on Friday
Assistant: Okay, printing twenty copies on normal paper now.
Person: can you also fax the poster to my brother?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send faxes. I can email him a scan if you give me his address.
Person: no worries. the weather is mild this week so i think we will get a crowd
Assistant: That sounds nice. The prints are ready.

name: break_timer
does: Starts a timer for your work and tells you when to take a short rest, so you can enjoy a tasty snack or stretch your legs.
inputs: how long to work and how long to rest
people say:
- Remind me to take a break in an hour.
- Work for twenty-five minutes, then tell me to stop.
- I want a focus timer.
- Give me a rest every half hour so I can drink a glass of water.
- Tell me when to stand up. I want to finish this before I plant the beans.

A navigation app shows you the way from one place to another. It uses maps and live traffic to tell you how long a drive will take. Your phone may upload its position every few seconds, so the app can warn you about a jam ahead. People change the plan in simple words: "Take the fastest route," "Avoid the highway," "Add a stop for fuel," or "How long until I get there?" If you want to celebrate a friend's birthday and must arrive on time, you might ask, "Will I get there by six?" or "Do I have enough time to stop for a gift?"

name: drive_time_estimate
does: Uses the internet to find how long a drive will take with today's traffic, so you can leave on time and enjoy the trip.
inputs: the place you start and the place you want to go, and a constant internet connection for live traffic
people say:
- How long to get to work?
- Is there a lot of traffic on the way to grandma's?
- What time should I leave to reach the lake by noon?
- How far is the beach?
- Will the drive take longer than usual this morning?

Nina had just woken up on Sunday morning. Her eyes were still closed when she said to the phone by her bed, "Find me a bike route of about twenty-five kilometres, and not too hilly." The assistant understood that she wanted a flat ride of that length. It showed a route along the river and said it would take about ninety minutes at a normal speed. "Switch to the quiet roads," said Nina, "I don't like cars." The assistant changed the route to a path with fewer cars. Nina said, "A dozen of us are meeting at the bridge at nine. Remind me at eight." The assistant saved the route and set the reminder for eight.

Someone wants the car warmed up before they leave.
Warm up the car.
Start the engine, I'm leaving in ten minutes.
Get the car warm, it's freezing.
Please turn on the heater in my car, because my mom is coming with me and she gets cold easily.
Increase the heat a bit, the morning air is sharp.
Start the car in five minutes. No, make that ten.
Start the engine at seven. Actually, make it seven thirty.
Could you please warm up the car for me before I come out?

Someone wants the front door locked for the night.
Lock up.
Good night, lock the front door, please.
Lock the front door and turn off the porch light.
It's bedtime, so please lock the doors.
Is the door locked? If not, lock it.
I'm heading to bed, so lock the front door and check the garage too.
Can you make sure everything is locked before I join the kids upstairs?

Someone wants the lights to come on at a certain time.
Lights on at seven.
Turn the kitchen lamp on tomorrow at seven.
Switch on the porch light when it gets dark.
I will be home at six, so have the hall light on by then.
I am not well tonight, so please keep the bedroom light on until nine.
Please note that I'm planting seeds early tomorrow, so turn on the garden light at five thirty.
Make the bedroom lights come on slowly in the morning.

Ali had moved to the city in February and still did not know where anything was. On Friday evening he dusted off his good coat and asked his phone, "What movies are on tonight near me? Nothing longer than two hours." The assistant looked up the nearby cinemas. It found three films, and the shortest one ran for ninety minutes. It read out the times, and said the cinema was ten minutes away by bus. Ali chose the one with the pale blue poster, a comedy, and said, "Show me the trailer first." The assistant played the trailer. Ali laughed and said, "Okay, the half past eight one." The assistant showed him the way and said the bus left in five minutes.

name: seating_planner
does: Makes a seating chart for a party so every guest has a seat, and lets you shift people around.
inputs: the guest names and the number of tables
people say:
- Where should everyone sit at the party?
- Put Aunt Rosa next to my cousin, but away from the speakers.
- Move Dan to table two.
- I need a seat plan for our yearly family dinner.
- Shift the kids to the table by the window.

Someone wants to know what twenty plus ten is.
Twenty plus ten?
What is twenty and ten together?
Add twenty and ten for me.
How much is ten more than twenty?
Quick, I'm in bed and can't do sums. What do twenty and ten make?
Zoom through this for me: twenty plus ten.
I'm in a silent library, so show it on the screen: twenty plus ten.

Person: Heater off.
Assistant: Sure. Do you mean the living room heater or the bedroom one?
Person: Both. Hurry, I'm late.
Assistant: Both heaters are off now.
Person: Notify me at six if the oven is still on.
Assistant: I can't see the oven, because it is not a smart one. I can remind you at six to check it, though.
Person: Fine. I'm cooking and I forgot one ingredient, so I need to run out.
Assistant: Okay. Thanks for being patient with me. I will remind you at six.

name: trail_distance_check
does: Tells you how long a hiking trail is, how many meters it climbs, and tags the steep parts.
inputs: the name of the trail and how fast you walk
people say:
- How long is the lake trail?
- Can we finish the ridge walk in half a day?
- How many kilometres is it to the top?
- Is the path to the waterfall steep?
- I need to know how hard the forest loop is before I pack.

Carlos was a gardener with dirty hands and a tight schedule. He knelt by the roses and said to his phone, "Could you please play the next chapter of my audiobook and make it a little faster? My hands are covered in soil, so I can't unlock the screen myself, and I want to finish this chapter before I have to pay the water bill at noon." The assistant heard his voice, unlocked the phone, found the book where he had stopped, and started chapter nine at one and a quarter speed. Carlos kept digging while the story played. At eleven thirty he said, "Pause it now, please." The assistant paused it and saved his place.

Watering is the main job in a garden. Plants need water, sun and time. A sprinkler connects to a hose and sprays water over the grass. Many people set a timer so it waters early in the morning, when the sun is low. Too much water is bad for most plants, and too little is bad too. People change things in simple words: "Water the tomatoes less," "Run the sprinkler for ten minutes," "Skip today, it's raining," or "Move watering to six." If you have an appointment in the morning, you might say, "Water after I leave."

Person: Remind me about my history homework.
Assistant: Sure. When should I remind you?
Person: Not tonight. I don't want to think about it until tomorrow.
Assistant: Okay. What time tomorrow?
Person: After school, around four. Can you also explain the homework to me? I'm sitting on the rug and I don't get it.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see your homework, so I can't explain it. If you read me the question, I can try to help. I set the reminder for four tomorrow.
Person: Can you make that reminder permanent, every day?
Assistant: Yes, I will repeat it every school day.

name: lost_pet_notice
does: Posts a short notice to the neighbourhood group when a pet is missing, and tells you when someone replies, so you are ready to welcome your pet home.
inputs: the pet's name, a photo, and where it was last seen
people say:
- My cat is gone. Tell the neighbours.
- Our dog ran out of the gate, can you let everyone know?
- Post a notice, Max is missing.
- We just came back from a trip and the rabbit is not in its cage. Ask the street to look.
- Tell everyone nearby to watch for a small grey cat.

Maya woke up with a cough and a heavy head. She did not remember what day it was, so she said to her speaker, "Is it bin day today? I don't want the garden waste, only the recycling." The assistant checked the calendar for her street and said the recycling truck would come at eight, and the garden waste was next week. Maya asked, "What goes in the blue bin again?" The assistant said paper, cans and clean plastic. Maya said, "Print the bin days for the month so I can put them on the fridge." The assistant sent the page to the printer. Maya dragged the bin to the road, happy that she had made it in time.

A calendar helps you remember what happens and when. You put events on it: meetings, birthdays, trips. Some events repeat every week, like a class on Sunday. A calendar can be private or public, and a public one can be seen by many people, like a school's calendar. People change events often: "Move my meeting to Tuesday," "What am I doing on Friday?" "Cancel lunch," or "Make the dentist an hour earlier." You can also write small tasks, like "buy milk," with a reminder. When two events happen at the same time, the calendar shows a warning.

Phones make it easy to record video. You press a button, film for a while, and stop. Many people film small things: a child at a birthday party, ice cream starting to melt in the sun, or a cooking clip of an apple pie. You can watch the clip, cut off the start, share it with a friend, or save it. People change settings too: "Record in wide mode," "Make the clip shorter," "Turn the sound off," or "Send it to Mum." Long videos use more storage, so people often ask, "How much space is left?"

A smoke alarm listens for smoke and makes a loud sound to wake people up. Some alarms are connected to the house wire, and others use a small battery that needs changing once a year. If the power goes out, people look for a torch and keep the fridge shut, because raw food and milk can go bad after a few hours. In an emergency, people say, "Call for help," "Call the fire service," or "Turn on the torch." They can also adjust things, like "Make the alarm quieter after the test" or "Remind me to change the battery in spring."

Someone wants to play the next episode of a podcast.
Next episode.
Play the next one.
Carry on with my podcast.
Keep going from where I stopped.
Play the episode about the north of England, the one about the summer heat.
I plan to listen on the train tomorrow at seven, so get the next episode ready.
Please could you start the following episode of my podcast? I have a long drive tomorrow at seven and I want it ready.

name: world_clock
does: Automatically tells you what time it is in another city, so you know if it is too late to call.
inputs: the name of a city
people say:
- What time is it in Tokyo?
- Is it morning in Lima yet?
- Pull up the time in Paris.
- It's six here. Is it too late to call the boiler company in Chicago?
- Time in New York right now?

Ruth was a retired teacher who sat by the window playing her guitar. Her old dog, Bruno, sat by his empty bowl and looked at her. Ruth put the guitar down and said to the smart speaker, "Ask the feeder to give Bruno his dinner straight away, but no treats tonight. The vet said he's had too many." The assistant understood that she wanted one normal meal and no treats. It told the feeder to fill the bowl, and it said the portion was one cup. "Good," said Ruth. "And don't let me forget his walk. Remind me at six." The assistant set a reminder for six. Bruno ate his dinner, and Ruth picked up her guitar again.

name: door_lock_timer
does: Locks a door at the time you choose, which reduces the chance of leaving it open.
inputs: which door and what time
people say:
- Lock the front door at ten every night.
- I'm silly and always forget, so lock up for me.
- Make sure the back door is locked when I go out on Saturday morning.
- Lock up for the night at eleven.
- Don't let the door stay open after I leave.

Finding a film to watch is easy. People look at what is on television or on the cinema list. They ask things like "What's on tonight?" "Show me comedies," or "When is the film at the cinema?" A trailer is a short video that shows a little of the film. If you want to watch later, you can download a film to your phone before a trip. Be patient, because a big film may take a while on slow wifi. People change their plans in simple words: "Play it from the start," "Show something shorter," or "Find a film for kids."

Yuki was new to the city and wanted to know what was going on. While the kitchen tap dripped, she said to her phone, "Tell me the local news, but I don't want sports or the weather. Keep it short." The assistant understood that she wanted only town news, in a short summary. It read three headlines: a new bus line, a street market on Saturday, and a road that would be closed. Yuki said, "I didn't hear the last one, say it again." The assistant repeated it. She said, "Tell me the news every morning at seven." The assistant set a daily short news update for seven. Yuki smiled and went to fix the tap.
